analysis.title: The Systematic Investor Report: Positive playbook performance: picking pockets of persistence
key_insights: Selling equity tail risk offered the best risk-adjusted performance YTD. S&P tail variance returned 12.5% YTD with a return/vol ratio of 5.52.

Equity volatility selling has been resilient, with uncertainty progressively priced into the downside tails. S&P tail variance made a positive return last Friday and Nasdaq gap risk declined very modestly.
A cautious market testing the upside has kept the S&P upside vol risk premium flat this year (S&P upside vol carry +0.1% YTD).
Selling USDJPY gap risk has printed a new performance high every month, as pricing gave an adequate buffer against several sources of uncertainty. JPY gap risk is +1.9% YTD.
FX carry did well in H1 but turned down after the Brazilian election and as rate differentials weighed on MXN. It is -1.5% over 1M and +6.5% YTD.
Trend-following has been an effective way to manage beta this year. Commodity trend is +17.3% YTD on energy- and climate-related disruption, and cross-asset trend is +5.7% YTD.
Rates trend helped in September. Commodity basis-momentum printed a new high in October per the text, though the performance table shows SGCMBM01 at -12.7% YTD and -4.5% over 1M.

Single-stock volatility and dispersion helped long-short strategies deliver positive YTD performance. Equity multi-factor returns were steady, while mean-reversion returns were more volatile as correlation dynamics shifted.

Long longer-maturity rates volatility helped portfolios in September across USD, EUR and JPY, and gave back some returns in October. Long rates spot vol is +3.8% YTD and long rates fwd vol is +4.6% YTD.
Combining long rates vol with short-dated vol carry added returns through the year.
US equity hedges have generally lost in a steady market (dynamic put spread US -1.7% YTD, dynamic long VIX -4.5% YTD). SG continues to prefer Synthetic Down Variance for tail protection.
The US midterms may add useful uncertainty and boost premia in short-dated options, alongside tech stock-driven volatility.
